description.narrative: ltpgtSyria remains highly vulnerable to sudden-onset emergencies caused by escalating hostilities, new displacement, natural disasters (e.g. floods, storms, earthquakes), or localized acute incidents. These risks are particularly severe in underserved rural and peri-urban areas of Rural Damascus, Homs, Lattakia, Al-Hassakeh, and Al-Raqqa, where fragile infrastructure, socio-economic instability, and vulnerable populations exacerbate humanitarian needs.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTo address these critical needs, the Syrian Society for Social Development (SSSD) has developed a flexible, multi-sectoral contingency response plan—aligned with the SHF Envelope 3 mechanism—that can be activated within 48 hours of a verified crisis, with all expenses and activities subject to Fund Manager approval and strictly limited to rapid, targeted interventions in acute emergencies,ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn the event of such emergencies, displaced and at-risk households often lack access to safe shelter, essential household items, adequate heating, and immediate food assistance. This results in heightened exposure to health risks, protection concerns, and further displacement. In particular, affected families frequently resort to overcrowded shelters, unfinished buildings, or public spaces without access to basic services.ltbrgtThe proposed intervention aims to address urgent needs in the initial phase of an emergency by delivering life-saving, multi-sectoral assistance across SNFI FSS sectors including Shelter options (prepare collective shelter, temporary preparation and use of public facilities like schools …etc. Non-Food Items (NFIs), Cash-for-Rent (CFR), Cash Top-Ups, RTEs, and Food Basket, to support the displaced and host families.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe response will be triggered by:ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtSudden displacement due to conflict or violence.lt/ligtltligtEscalation of hostilities or bombardments in civilian areas.lt/ligtltligtNatural disasters (e.g. flooding, storms, earthquakes, …etc).lt/ligtltligtAlerts from CCCM and Protection partners, local authorities, or OCHA-led coordination mechanisms.ltbrgtlt/ligtltligtOther acute incidents resulting in urgent, multi-sectoral humanitarian needs.lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtThe project will be further detailed upon activation of the rapid emergency response mechanism and will include specific geographic areas, results from rapid needs assessments, bills of quantities (BoQs), and other technical details in line with SHF procedures.lt/pgt
